commenter_information.author_organization_name: Oracle Health and Life Sciences; signed by Alex Mugge, Sr. Director, Global Health Policy & Regulatory Intelligence
commenter_information.credentials_or_expertise_mentioned: Leading supplier of EHR, clinical and revenue cycle information systems, population health, clinical research, and interoperability solutions; actively developing HL7 FHIR Da Vinci ePA functionality for EHR customers.

executive_summary: Oracle Health strongly supports NCPDP standards for pharmacy-benefit drug ePA and supports adopting Da Vinci CRD, DTR, and PAS version 2.2 for medical services and medical-benefit drugs. It recommends eliminating the January 1, 2027 non-version-specific FHIR ePA milestone and instead requiring Da Vinci 2.2 by July 1, 2027, with ONC certification alignment and 2027 treated as a transition/bonus year. Oracle urges CMS not to require CDex, FAST Security, or Tiered OAuth yet, supports FHIR-based HIPAA PA modernization with a broad referral-related definition, and recommends using production adoption thresholds, SVAP, and flexible early implementation rules to manage standards maturity.

detailed_positions.rationale: NCPDP standards are widely implemented, proven in production, adopted under Medicare Part D, and understood by providers, pharmacies, PBMs, and plans.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Finalize NCPDP standards as the primary mechanism for pharmacy-benefit drug prior authorization and avoid competing frameworks.

detailed_positions.topic: Da Vinci v2.2 for medical services and medical-benefit drugs
detailed_positions.rationale: Da Vinci 2.2 reflects lessons learned and improves consistency over versions 2.0 and 2.1, but still needs refinement from deployment experience.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Adopt CRD v2.2.1, DTR v2.2.0, and PAS v2.2.1 as the common baseline; eliminate the January 1, 2027 non-version-specific deadline; require v2.2 by July 1, 2027; use SVAP and future rulemaking to raise the floor later.

detailed_positions.rationale: Payers, providers, and HIT developers need to work from the same IG versions to reduce implementation variation and burden.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Adopt Da Vinci 2.2 into ONC certification, expire version 2.0 on the final rule effective date, approve v2.2 via SVAP as soon as possible, and let 2027 operate as a transition/bonus year.

detailed_positions.rationale: Most cases can be inferred from order type, but edge cases require better automation and may be complicated by payer-specific benefits and formularies.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Do not delay drug ePA standards over edge cases; use order type for current workflow; collaborate with Da Vinci, NCPDP, and stakeholders to enhance CRD CoverageInformation for long-term automated workflow determination; do not require CRD for all medication requests yet.

detailed_positions.rationale: CDex is useful for additional information exchange but has limited or no production use in PA and is not critical while PAS can carry initial supporting information.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Do not require the capability to request/share additional information after initial PA; recommend CDex only for voluntary implementers following PAS guidance; do not put CDex in the critical path for initial ePA scaling.

detailed_positions.topic: FAST Security IG and Tiered OAuth
detailed_positions.rationale: FAST SSRAA and Tiered OAuth are immature and not widely adopted, especially outside network environments.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Encourage exploration of FAST Security and SMART App Launch compatibility, but do not require FAST Security or Tiered OAuth until substantial testing and adoption occur.

detailed_positions.rationale: FHIR Maturity Model and ONC ISA do not sufficiently measure production implementation readiness.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Use real-world adoption thresholds, generally at least 10,000 providers across settings and 100 health plans for IG regulatory adoption; for FAST Security testing, Oracle also references a lower guideline of at least 1,000 providers and 100 health plans.

detailed_positions.rationale: FHIR-based approaches can integrate more deeply into provider workflows than existing X12 transactions; temporary dual-standard burden is justified by long-term benefits.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Adopt FHIR standards for prior authorization and support the alternative to cover full 45 CFR 162.1301 referral certification/authorization transactions; include 162.1301(b) referral-related authorization; adopt CRD/DTR/PAS, US Core, SMART App Launch, and FHIR R4; manage future versions through SVAP.

detailed_positions.rationale: Removing portal/direct data entry too early could increase burden and create inability to handle some real-world cases, though future removal may drive API adoption.
detailed_positions.specific_request: State intent to revisit the exception later; do not remove it now; when removed, apply the change only to prior authorization transactions, potentially around 2029.

detailed_positions.topic: Payer API oversight and certification RFI
detailed_positions.rationale: Interactive PA workflows need conformance and predictability, but certification could differ from EHR certification and should minimize burden.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Develop automated testing/attestation or validation approaches, prioritize Prior Authorization API validation on both payer and provider HIT sides, and explicitly allow reasonable implementation variations during early real-world adoption.

solicitation_responses.summary: Strongly supports requiring Da Vinci CRD, DTR, and PAS v2.2 as the common ePA foundation.
Supports adoption of CRD v2.2.1, DTR v2.2.0, and PAS v2.2.1 and ONC certification alignment.
Recommends using ONC SVAP and rulemaking to manage future post-2.2 versions while maintaining v2.2 as the regulatory floor.
Supports requiring impacted payers to incorporate coverage and documentation requirements into the Prior Authorization API for medical-benefit drugs.
Strongly supports NCPDP standards for pharmacy-benefit drug ePA.
Says the medical/pharmacy distinction needs work but should not delay finalization; recommends order type as current-state approach and future CRD enhancements.
Supports requiring v2.2 ePA IGs but urges implementation flexibility because v2.2 still needs refinement.
Recommends eliminating January 1, 2027 and requiring v2.2 by July 1, 2027 rather than October 1, 2027.
States RTPB is prevalent in clinical workflow but not commonly used for PA; F&B is more commonly used to indicate whether PA is required.
Says CRD CoverageInformation can theoretically indicate benefit path but needs vocabulary enhancements and should not be required for all medication requests yet.
Discusses workflow integration challenges, especially DTR integration into clinician workflow and PAS shift from back-end batch to real-time review.
Supports FHIR as HIPAA PA standard, supports including referral-related authorization, recognizes dual X12/FHIR transition burden, and recommends SVAP-based version management.
Supports robust testing/validation and explores payer API certification or automated attestation, especially for Prior Authorization API interactions.
Supports replacing earlier CRD/DTR/PAS versions with v2.2, expiring v2.0 on the final rule effective date, and using SVAP for future updates.
Responds to API technology oversight/certification RFIs and direct data entry exception questions.

overall_position: Strong support with targeted technical modifications and maturity safeguards.
notes: Major HIT vendor comment emphasizing rapid alignment on Da Vinci 2.2, ONC certification coordination, and avoiding premature requirements for CDex/FAST/Tiered OAuth.
